t.p: Edo period onward (wide ripsaws from 1763); higonokami 1896–present

t.d: Natural Japanese waterstones (tennen toishi) quarried for finishing blades, used wet.

t.d: France's main cutlery centre, making about 70% of the country's cutting tools, including laguiole and Douk-Douk knives.
t.tech: forged or stamped blades, slip-joint assembly
t.mat: carbon and stainless steel, horn, wood
t.auth: 'Laguiole' is not a protected name; French makers stamp their mark, steel or 'Made in France' on the blade.

t.d: Swedish forges making hand-forged axes, each signed by its smith.
t.auth: smith's initials stamped on each head

t.d: Slim French slip-joint pocket knife with a tapered blade and ornamented backspring.
t.tech: slip-joint assembly, forged or stamped blade
t.mat: cattle horn, wood, aluminium; stainless or carbon steel (XC75, XC100)
t.auth: 'Laguiole' is a generic name, not a protected one; French makers often stamp their mark and steel type on the blade.

t.tech: grinding on water-powered stones; crucible steel

t.d: German cutlery centre known for swords, knives, scissors and razors; home to Zwilling J. A. Henckels and Böker.

t.p: Carpentry first developed in the 12th century
